## Figure S2

```{r}
#| label: fig-pollutant-maps-qlog10
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Spatial maps of ", analysis_end_year, " emissions for each GHG and pollutant, aggregated across AIS-broadcasting vessels and non-broadcasting vessels, and shown at a 1x1 degree spatial resolution. Emissions are area-normalized for each pixel (metric tonnes per square kilometer) and shown using a log-10 scale. Each panel is scaled independently, spanning the ", scales::ordinal(pollutant_map_lower_quantile * 100), " percentile to the maximum of that pollutant, with lower values drawn in the darkest colour; colours are therefore not comparable between panels.")'
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8

pollutant_map_data_all <- total_spatial_emissions_by_pollutant_formatted |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pollutant = dplyr::case_when(
      pollutant == "CO2" ~ "CO[2]",
      pollutant == "N2O" ~ "N[2]*O",
      pollutant == "CH4" ~ "CH[4]",
      pollutant == "PM2.5" ~ "PM[2.5]",
      pollutant == "PM10" ~ "PM[10]",
      pollutant == "SOX" ~ "SO[X]",
      pollutant == "NOX" ~ "NO[X]",
      TRUE ~ pollutant
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pollutant = forcats::fct_relevel(pollutant, pollutant_factor_levels)
  )

# Where each pollutant's colour scale starts, as a quantile of its own pixels.
# Nearly every pixel of these maps sits far below 1 MT/km2, so a scale running
# from the bottom of the distribution spends almost all of its range on trace
# values and washes the shipping lanes out. Starting high and squishing (rather
# than dropping) everything below the cut puts the low-emission ocean at the dark
# end of magma, the same way the other emissions maps read.
pollutant_map_lower_quantile <- 0.75

# scales::label_log() assumes breaks sit on decades. The default break algorithm
# falls back to fractional exponents when a pollutant spans only a couple of
# decades, which prints labels like 10^-2.523, so pick the decades directly.
decade_breaks <- function(limits) {
  breaks <- 10^seq(ceiling(log10(limits[1])), floor(log10(limits[2])))
  if (length(breaks) < 2) scales::breaks_log()(limits) else breaks
}

pollutant_map_list <- purrr::map(
  unique(pollutant_map_data_all$pollutant),
  function(pollutant_tmp) {
    pollutant_tmp <- as.character(pollutant_tmp)

    pollutant_map_data <- pollutant_map_data_all |>
      dplyr::filter(pollutant == pollutant_tmp)

    scale_limits <- pollutant_map_data |>
      dplyr::summarize(
        min = quantile(
          .data[[map_end_col]],
          pollutant_map_lower_quantile,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        max = max(.data[[map_end_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
      ) |>
      as.numeric()

    pollutant_map_data |>
      ggplot() +
      geom_sf(
        data = world_bbox_sf,
        fill = emissions_map_ocean_color
      ) +
      ggspatial::geom_spatial_tile(
        aes(
          x = lon_bin + 0.5,
          y = lat_bin + 0.5,
          color = .data[[map_end_col]],
          fill = .data[[map_end_col]]
        )
      ) +
      geom_sf(
        data = land,
        color = emissions_map_land_color,
        fill = emissions_map_land_color
      ) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(
        # units are given once in the caption, so the nine panels do not repeat
        # the same legend title
        name = NULL,
        option = "magma",
        limits = scale_limits,
        # clamp the low tail onto the darkest colour instead of censoring it
        oob = scales::squish,
        trans = "log10",
        breaks = decade_breaks,
        na.value = emissions_map_ocean_color,
        labels = scales::label_log()
      ) +
      scale_color_viridis_c(
        # units are given once in the caption, so the nine panels do not repeat
        # the same legend title
        name = NULL,
        option = "magma",
        limits = scale_limits,
        # clamp the low tail onto the darkest colour instead of censoring it
        oob = scales::squish,
        trans = "log10",
        breaks = decade_breaks,
        na.value = emissions_map_ocean_color,
        labels = scales::label_log()
      ) +
      labs(x = "", y = "") +
      theme_void() +
      guides(
        fill = guide_colorbar(
          title.position = "top",
          title.hjust = 0.5,
          frame.colour = emissions_map_frame_color,
          ticks.colour = emissions_map_frame_color
        )
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 1)) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 1)) +
      theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.direction = "horizontal",
        legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm")
      ) +
      facet_wrap(pollutant ~ ., labeller = label_parsed)
  }
)

cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = pollutant_map_list, ncol = 3)
```

```{r}
make_pollutant_time_series_figure <- function(
  pollutant_time_series_data,
  y_axis_label
) {
  {
    ggplot(
      data = pollutant_time_series_data,
      aes(x = month, y = emissions_mt)
    ) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
      theme_plot() +
      labs(x = "", y = y_axis_label) +
      theme(
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0)
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = seq(
          lubridate::ymd(glue::glue("{analysis_start_year}-01-01")),
          lubridate::ymd(glue::glue("{analysis_end_year+1}-01-01")),
          by = "1 year"
        ),
        labels = seq(analysis_start_year, analysis_end_year + 1)
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), labels = scales::comma)
  }
}

) +
  facet_wrap(
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-emissions-by-country-and-activity-type
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("CO$_{2}$ emissions by country for AIS-broadcasting vessels during different activity types (international trips, port stays, and domestic trips), aggregated for activities ending in ", analysis_end_year, ". Emissions for each international trip are partitioned equally to its departure and arrival country. The color scale is square-root transformed, so that lower-emitting countries remain distinguishable alongside the largest emitters. Countries with no values are shown in gray.")'
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 8

all_port_and_trip_emissions_without_vessel_class <- all_port_and_trip_emissions |>
  dplyr::group_by(country_iso3, type) |>
  dplyr::summarise(emissions_co2_mt = sum(emissions_co2_mt)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()


all_countries_for_plot <- land |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::select(country_iso3) |>
  tidyr::crossing(
    all_port_and_trip_emissions_without_vessel_class |>
      dplyr::distinct(type)
  )

port_trip_emissions_fig <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = world_bbox_sf,
    fill = emissions_map_ocean_color,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = all_countries_for_plot |>
      dplyr::left_join(land, by = "country_iso3") |>
      dplyr::left_join(
        all_port_and_trip_emissions_without_vessel_class,
        by = c("country_iso3", "type")
      ) |>
      sf::st_as_sf(),
    aes(fill = emissions_co2_mt),
    # enough weight to separate neighbouring countries and the coastline
    color = "grey55",
    linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  facet_wrap(type ~ ., ncol = 1) +
  coord_sf(crs = map_projection) +
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    # A different palette family from the gridded emissions maps on purpose: this
    # is a choropleth of country totals, not a spatial field, and mako's cool
    # blue-greens keep the two kinds of map from being read as the same thing.
    # Run bright-for-more over the same black ocean as those maps, and start
    # above mako's black end so the lowest-emitting countries still separate
    # from the ocean behind them.
    #
    # Square-root rather than linear: China emits an order of magnitude more
    # than the median country, so a linear scale collapses everyone else into
    # the bottom of the ramp. sqrt lifts the mid-tier countries clear while
    # still leaving China visibly the maximum - pseudolog10, which the gridded
    # pollutant maps use, over-corrects here and flattens the ranking.
    option = "mako",
    direction = 1,
    begin = 0.2,
    trans = "sqrt",
    labels = scales::unit_format(unit = "M", scale = 1e-6),
    na.value = emissions_map_land_color
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    fill = bquote(.(analysis_end_year) ~ CO[2] ~ emissions ~ (MT)),
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_colorbar(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      frame.colour = emissions_map_frame_color,
      ticks.colour = emissions_map_frame_color
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.key.width = unit(1.75, "cm")
  )

port_trip_emissions_fig
```

## Table S6

```{r}
#| results: 'asis'
# Companion to Figure S4: the leading countries behind each activity type, with
# every country outside the top few pooled into a single "Other" row
n_countries_shown <- 30

top_countries_by_activity_type <- all_port_and_trip_emissions_without_vessel_class |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    country = countrycode::countrycode(
      country_iso3,
      "iso3c",
      "country.name",
      warn = FALSE
    ),
    # a handful of codes have no country name; keep the code itself for those
    country = dplyr::coalesce(country, country_iso3)
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    emissions_co2_mt = sum(emissions_co2_mt),
    .by = c(type, country)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    country_rank = dplyr::min_rank(dplyr::desc(emissions_co2_mt)),
    .by = type
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    country = dplyr::if_else(
      country_rank > n_countries_shown,
      "Other",
      country
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    emissions_co2_mt = sum(emissions_co2_mt),
    # the pooled row keeps the rank of its best member, which sorts it last
    country_rank = min(country_rank),
    .by = c(type, country)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(type, country_rank)

# One column pair per activity type, ranked down the page
top_countries_by_activity_type_kable <- top_countries_by_activity_type |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    emissions_co2_mt = scales::label_number(
      scale = 1e-6,
      accuracy = 0.1
    )(emissions_co2_mt),
    table_row = dplyr::row_number(),
    .by = type
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = table_row,
    names_from = type,
    values_from = c(country, emissions_co2_mt),
    names_vary = "slowest"
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-table_row) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "latex",
    label = "top_countries_by_activity_type",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", "r", "l", "r", "l", "r"),
    col.names = rep(c("Country", "CO$_{2}$"), 3),
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = paste0(
      "Top ",
      n_countries_shown,
      " countries by ",
      analysis_end_year,
      " CO$_{2}$ emissions (millions of metric tonnes) from AIS-broadcasting vessels, shown separately for each activity type, with all remaining countries pooled into a single Other row. Emissions for each international trip are partitioned equally to its departure and arrival country. These are the totals mapped in Figure \\ref{fig:fig-emissions-by-country-and-activity-type}."
    )
  ) |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(
    c(
      "International trips" = 2,
      "Port stays" = 2,
      "Domestic trips" = 2
    )
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    # No "scale_down" here. It wraps the tabular in \resizebox, and sn-jnl.cls
    # redefines the table environment to put its body inside threeparttable;
    # the two together error out ("\begin{threeparttable} ... ended by
    # \end{tabular}"), so LaTeX silently drops the whole float. The table then
    # never appears in the PDF and \ref{tab:top_countries_by_activity_type}
    # renders as ??. font_size 7 already fits the six columns in \linewidth
    # with no overfull box, so the resizebox bought us nothing.
    font_size = 7,
    latex_options = "hold_position"
  )

top_countries_by_activity_type_kable

top_countries_by_activity_type_kable |>
  writeLines(
    file.path(project_root, "tables", "top_countries_by_activity_type.tex")
  )
```

```{r}
    flag = countrycode::countrycode(
      flag,
      origin = "iso3c",
      destination = "country.name"
    )
  ) |>
  # Don't include unknown receiver type
  dplyr::filter(receiver_type != "unknown") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    receiver_type = stringr::str_to_sentence(receiver_type) |>
      forcats::fct_relevel("Satellite", "Terrestrial", "Dynamic")
  ) |>
  # Fill in missing values with 0s
  tidyr::complete(
    receiver_type,
    tidyr::nesting(year, flag),
    fill = list(emissions_co2_mt = 0, n_distinct_ssvid = 0)
  ) |>
  # Cap at the analysis end year
  dplyr::filter(year <= analysis_end_year)

top_n_flags <- annual_global_emissions_by_receiver_type_and_flag |>
  dplyr::filter(year == analysis_end_year, receiver_type == "Total") |>
  dplyr::slice_max(n = 10, order_by = emissions_co2_mt) |>
  dplyr::select(flag)

annual_global_emissions_by_receiver_type_and_flag |>
  dplyr::inner_join(top_n_flags, by = "flag") |>
  dplyr::mutate(flag = forcats::fct_relevel(flag, top_n_flags$flag)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = emissions_co2_mt, color = flag)) +
  facet_grid(receiver_type ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::unit_format(unit = "M", scale = 1e-6)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = unique(annual_global_emissions_by_receiver_type_and_flag$year)
  ) +
  theme_plot() +
  labs(x = "", y = expression(CO[2] ~ emissions ~ (MT)), color = "Flag") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2022, linetype = 2) +
  paletteer::scale_color_paletteer_d(palette = "rcartocolor::Safe")
```
